draft.title: Specific heat capacity in physics
card: Specific heat capacity (c) is the energy needed to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1 °C. Its unit is J/(kg °C).
The energy to change an object's temperature is Q = mcΔT. Q is energy in joules, m is mass in kg, and ΔT is the change in temperature.
For the same mass and the same energy, a substance with a low c warms up more than one with a high c. Water has a high c, about 4200 J/(kg °C).
ΔT is final temperature minus initial temperature. It is negative when the object cools, so Q is then negative and energy leaves the object.
draft.remember: Q = mcΔT: more mass or a higher c means more energy is needed for the same temperature change.

a.q: Two blocks of equal mass gain the same energy. Block X has a lower c than block Y. Which statement is correct?
opts: Block X warms up by more than block Y
Block Y warms up by more than block X
Both blocks warm up by the same amount
Block X needs more energy for the same rise
a.why: With Q and m equal, ΔT = Q ÷ (mc), so a lower c gives a larger ΔT. Block Y is tempting only if you think a higher c means more warming, but a high c means the block resists temperature change.
a.clue: Rearrange the formula to find ΔT.

b.q: Ayesha heats 2.0 kg of water in a pan in Geelong from 20 °C to 30 °C. Water has c = 4200 J/(kg °C). How much energy does the water gain?
b.why: Q = mcΔT = 2.0 × 4200 × 10 = 84 000 J. The value 42 000 J comes from leaving out the mass of 2.0 kg.
b.clue: ΔT is the change in temperature, not the final temperature.

a.best: Block X warms up by more than block Y
